assessments.reasoning: PDF page 270 is addressed to Visual Basic 6.0 users and places the described changes against earlier Visual Basic versions using the Visual Basic .NET 2002 boundary. Page 284 supplies an explicit source-edition column, supporting membership of the named VB6 language edition in the historical line.

challenge.method: Cross-read the migration heading and VB6 source column with Microsoft's release history (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/visual-basic/whats-new/) and its distinct VBA and VB6 product-level uses (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/visualstudio/visual-basic-6/visual-basic-6-support-policy). Tested the reverse link and a possible Visual Studio 6.0 suite reading.
challenge.results: The archive treats VB6 as the earlier language edition whose users migrate. A suite or runtime reading cannot account for the source language types, and reversing the link would collapse the broader pre-2002 line into one edition.

limitations: The relationship uses the index's display label and the migration context. It establishes no uninterrupted compatibility across earlier releases.
